source: Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries (MAFF), General Directorate of Agriculture, Department of Agricultural Extension — 'បច្ចេកទេសដាំដំណាំឪឡឹក' (Watermelon Cultivation Techniques), 2017.
text:
Aphids are small sap-sucking insects that cluster mainly on the underside of young watermelon leaves and shoot tips, causing leaves to curl and become distorted. Beyond the direct feeding damage, aphids are important because they transmit Watermelon Mosaic virus from infected to healthy plants as they feed.

Prevention: plant with proper spacing to allow good air circulation, which discourages aphid buildup; inspect the field regularly (about once a week); and promptly remove weeds around the field, since weeds can serve as alternate hosts and a source of aphids. Where leaves are heavily infested, farmers are advised to cut off and remove those leaves from the field for disposal rather than leaving them scattered on the ground, to prevent aphids from spreading further.

Chemical control: insecticides containing Abamectin, Dinotefuran, Fipronil, or Lambdacyhalothrin can be sprayed to control aphid populations, following label instructions.
